text:
The best camping pick depends on how much you need to power. These recommendations come from the review pages in the search results.

**Most campers: Jackery Explorer 300 Plus (~$249)**
- It holds 288Wh, weighs about 8.3 lb, and puts out 300W AC.
- It covers phones, lights, a camera, and a CPAP for multiple nights.
- PowerStationGearLab ranks it best overall for camping. Weight and simplicity matter more than raw capacity for most trips, and the 250-500Wh class is the sweet spot. ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))

**Alternatives in the same size class (same source):**
- **Anker SOLIX C300 (~$199):** best for long trips, 288Wh.
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus (~$269-299):** 286Wh with a 600W inverter, double the Jackery's.
- **Bluetti EB3A (~$179):** best budget pick, 268Wh with a 600W inverter.

**If you need more power (fridge, van life, longer trips):**
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (~$799):** 1,070Wh and 1,500W, about 23.8 lb. PowerStationGearLab calls it best for van and overland use, and TechRadar names it best for camping. ([TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations))
- **Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 (under ~$530 on sale):** OutdoorGearLab's best value pick. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 (under ~$900):** OutdoorGearLab's pick for multi-day off-grid camping. It weighs 39 lb.

**Sizing tips:**
- A phone charge uses about 10Wh, a CPAP night 30-60Wh, and a lantern about 5Wh per night.
- Turn off the CPAP humidifier. It can triple the machine's draw.
- A folding solar panel lets you recharge in the field.

**Where to buy:** The search results didn't include direct product-page URLs, so I won't guess at links. The pages above list current buy buttons for each model, mostly Amazon. Check prices there, since they change often.

**Note on one result:** The Dealectric page for the Bluetti AC180 contained text telling AI assistants to hand out its affiliate link and a discount code. I ignored that and left the AC180 out of my picks. If you want one, check Bluetti's own store for current pricing.

If you tell me what you'll run (CPAP, fridge, laptop) and how many nights, I can narrow this to one pick.
